records.c: Briefing selection. The keyboard-free menu stores zero for Practice, one for North Pole, two for Sahara and three for New Orleans. Both the briefing and game setup use it to index course tables.
Three NOP bytes precede the disk loader's hand-over address at $0803.
Wait for raster synchronisation and blank the display, initialise the gameplay state and the title sequence, then configure the selected course and transfer to the main game through $2A00.

Presents the title and course briefing. Installs the menu raster interrupt, builds the title screen, starts sound cues, then waits for the briefing state and a fire press before handing control back to startup.
Synchronises at $09C9 and clears bit 4 of VIC control register $D011.
Sets VIC pointers to $1F in bank 1, sets multicolour character mode, disables CIA interrupt sources and installs the hardware vectors in RAM. Enables the raster interrupt and restores IRQ processing.
Interrupt return used by the vectors installed beside the menu IRQ. It preserves the registers by doing no work before the return.
Waits for the high raster region and low byte $30, then tests joystick fire on CIA1's port A mirror at $DC90. Returns A=1 only when fire is down and the score-slot selector at $B489 is eight.
Entry past raster synchronisation. Tests the active-low fire bit and requires $B489 to be eight.
Loads Y with two before falling into the raster-counting delay. The caller can start at $09ED with a different Y.
Uses X as a wrapping inner counter and the incoming Y as the outer count. The inner loop progresses while $D012 is zero.
Returns A=1 when port 2 fire first goes low and sets the latch at $0A16. A released button clears the latch, allowing another press.
One-byte latch set on the first sampled low fire signal and cleared by the first sampled release.
Countdown that delays opening the report after the ordinary course state signals an end.
Set by the title sequence to allow the menu IRQ to call the per-channel sound update at $98DD.
Copies five 38-cell strips and places decorative screen codes around them. Copies credits from $B730 and the copyright lines from $3FD0, $3FDC, $EFAF and $EFCC into the screen at $4400.
Selects briefing colours and starts clearing the screen at $4400. The course menu uses this panel to display the globe, course name and briefing text.
Lays out the repeating 40-cell panel strip from $0C61 and writes the frame's edge rows. The same panel builder is reused for the results display.
Returns from the panel and border drawing path.
Ten screen codes for TOP SECRET, copied to $4488 by the briefing panel builder.
Text immediately after the briefing heading, ending in $FF. It introduces the practice accuracy rating.
Screen-code strip used repeatedly by the briefing frame builder at $0BA5. The codes select the repeating panel and edge tiles in the active briefing character set.
Forty screen codes for the repeating top frame, including its multicolour trim and glyph breaks.
Forty panel screen codes for the contrasting lower trim and illuminated segments.
Shared return for the briefing input poll when neither a scroll update nor a fire edge is pending.

Switches between course selection and the scrolling description. On a new fire press, the North Pole and Sahara selections signal completion directly. The Practice and New Orleans selections initialise a scroll pointer and countdown.
Reloads a twelve-tick divider and checks the complete joystick port byte. Exactly $7D advances the course number and $7E decrements it. The selector wraps across four values.
Uses the course index to copy a 31-screen-code caption to $46AD and to select two addresses from the paired tables at $E000 and $E008.
Counts down a pacing byte before it draws a sliding window of text at $46FA. A $FF terminator at the final scroll position sets $0DF2.
Four bytes before the completion flag. This sequence includes the character's distance from the left of the display window at $0DEF and the scroll countdown at $0DF0.
Column at which the briefing writer starts displaying its cached text.
Counter reloaded with five between successive scroll updates.
Mutable byte cleared with the briefing flags at $0EDA.
Signals the foreground briefing loop to proceed past its final wait.
Selects the report or initials processing path inside the menu raster interrupt.
Four little-endian pointers selected by the course index for the description that scrolls across the briefing panel.
High-byte alias of the four course description pointers.
Four little-endian pointers selected by the course index for the title line copied at $0D96.
Indexed high half of the course-caption addresses.
X coordinate in each two-byte globe marker position.
Y coordinate in the same pairs. $ABBE subtracts the animation's offset from it.

Saves registers, sets the briefing palette and raster compare, then updates the audio and the briefing or score-entry state. Acknowledges VIC IRQ at $0E8A and uses the common interrupt return at $18C2.
Thirteen increasing bytes from $82 to $CC between the menu interrupt and its state block.
Value the menu IRQ writes to the VIC multicolour background register $D022.
Controls whether the IRQ calls the briefing drawing and selection updates.
Counts down before the IRQ starts testing the briefing fire edge.
Set to a nonzero value for the briefing scroll or readiness phase. The foreground loop at $0914 waits for this flag.
Countdown for the periodic effect path. The IRQ reloads it with six before requesting effect ten.
Countdown reloaded with twelve between samples of the directional selection input.
Clears screen cells across the report area and puts colour one into the matching rows before drawing text.
Clears title sequencer, score, display and mission flags before initialising the briefing. The zero stores include the briefing completion flag, the scroll enable and the shared sound gate.
Ten initial values copied into the course's projected state during the setup beginning at $0EC3.
Ten bytes paired with the preceding setup column and copied by the same initialisation loop.
Third ten-byte column of the projected state seed data.
Fourth ten-byte column of the projected state seed data.
The title procedure tests this byte before calling the initial graphics exchange and clears it afterwards.
Ten values including several low bytes of the projected bitmap parameters used at startup.
Ten high-page values paired with the preceding initial positions.

Clears the upper display and its colour rows. For Practice, copies the target-count header from $12E2. For the other courses it draws the score and high-score digits. It also configures the following raster stages.
Copies the mission start line into the two-row banner, draws the 240-cell dashboard from $A5E0 and initialises the fuel gauge, missile indicators and panel colours.
Loads the course's layout pointer from $B7BB. Decodes nonzero screen codes into three horizon rows, interpreting zero plus a count as a skip and $FF as the end.
Tile and text bytes for the red- and black-target counter headings shown above the practice course.
Forty-byte first Practice row copied by $10EE. It begins with the tiles that precede the visible RED TARGETS legend.
Screen-code fragment beginning the RED TARGETS label in the copied practice header. The surrounding row has paired digit tiles for the count.
First screen codes in the TARGET PRACTICE ASSESSMENT title. The fragment at $1311 supplies the remainder.
Title fragment for the practice assessment, ending just before the mission-start banner.
Screen codes for YOUR MISSION BEGINS. Copied to the display above the river.
Applies the course sky colour and tones for three horizon rows. Copies those rows to the three saved strips starting at $8330.
Configures RAM IRQ vector $1535 before starting the course raster chain, with the compare register initially zero.
RTS used as the target of stage-specific interrupt setup calls, separate from the hardware IRQ entry one byte later.

At the playfield split, writes bitmap-mode VIC control values, uploads sprite positions, pointers and colours, and schedules the HUD interrupt at $1535. Its guard compares $4A to the compare value installed by $1802.
Mutable low byte of the jump which skips a number of leading NOP cycles in the playfield handler.
High byte of the self-modified jump target used before the playfield interrupt's guarded VIC writes. $1EC1 computes both operand bytes from sprite Y positions.

Sets character-mode display parameters for the dashboard, captures sprite collision bits, scans the keyboard, updates secondary sprites and dispatches the lower-screen gameplay and sound work. It schedules $1829 at raster compare $28.
Reads CIA1 port B with port A driven low. Live matrix probe: no key reads $FF, Run/Stop reads $7F and reaches the pause increment, and Return reads $FD and reaches the abort store.
Last CIA1 port-B value read after selecting all keyboard columns at $1564.
Stores the speed index before pause and restores it when the pause key has been released and pressed again.
Bit mask ORed into the raster handlers' VIC control values to show or blank the display.
Set while the mission-start raster banner countdown is active.
Shadow for the first two high-X sprite bits, merged into the hardware value by the playfield IRQ.

Restores the normal CIA1 port-A mask after the keyboard test. Depending on the gameplay state, updates the speed needle, runs course events and projectiles, steps the smoothed speed and fuel, and then rejoins the raster chain.
X coordinate of the boat's first sprite layer, uploaded during the bitmap IRQ.
Horizontal coordinate for the second boat sprite layer and the remaining positions in its staging group.
Y coordinate uploaded with the first boat layer.
Y coordinate of the second layer. Indexed sprite updates address the following staging bytes with the same family of pointers.
Image selector for the first boat layer.
Image selector for the second layer, with adjacent pointers held in the same stage-specific row.
VIC colour value for the first layer where the raster uploads the boat.
Second layer colour copied to $D028 at $1414. The uses of the following bytes in this listing record remain open.
Sixteen results selected by the low nibble of the sum of the previous selector, two X positions and the CIA timer value.
Sets horizon colours and applies horizontal fine scroll. When fine scroll crosses a character boundary it moves three screen rows and supplies edge characters before scheduling $1802.
Restores sprite enables from $02E7 and schedules $1397 at raster compare $72.
Changes sky colour and uses $18E8 to time the mission banner. It modifies the top two screen rows, triggers a cue through $8600 and schedules $16F5 at raster compare $3B.
Pulls Y, X and A in that order and returns from the raster interrupt.

Raster countdown used to put up and remove the mission-start banner. Initial definite delay of two interrupts leads to a $FF-tick active count while $1614 is set.
Captured value from the VIC sprite-sprite collision register, used by the contact and projectile routines.
Mutable byte cleared with the raster and course state.
Byte cleared by the course initialiser at $0F1B.
State byte before the active horizon scroll flag.
Index into the three special horizon character streams. Zero selects the normal edge characters.
Countdown controlling when the special horizon stream advances to its next column.
Opening-state flag tested before the projectile and fuel updates. Cleared by the banner handler at $188C.
Count of remaining timed opening sound stages.
Divider decremented by the playfield handler before it advances the opening sound stage.
Triples of sprite pointers for the first wake phase. The offset incorporates steering position and the speed-dependent bank selected at $B202 or $B20A.
Second byte of each first-phase pointer triple, read by $B21F at the shared index.
Third byte of each first-phase triple, read by $B225. The engine applies all three pointers to stacked boat and wake sprites.
Companion three-pointer sequence used when the wake updater changes phase.
Second byte of each companion wake-pointer triple, copied at $B231.
Third byte of each companion triple, copied to $FFF6 at $B23A.
Uses the wave timer and saved pointers to erase an older mark. Projects the new location with the depth-to-Y table, river geometry and split bitmap row addresses before drawing the mark.
Mutable addend of the instruction at $19FE. Values $01 and $FF set the direction of the per-mark horizontal drift when the fractional movement overflows.
Mutable state before the water-mark cursor and depth arrays.
The current water-mark sprite or bitmap slot. The update advances through eight slots and wraps to zero.
One byte of scratch beside the water-mark update cursor.
Second scratch byte between the cursor and the projected position.
Base lateral displacement selected from the river row and its offset table.
Eight per-mark whole-pixel lateral offsets updated on carry from the fractional array.
Eight fractional lateral positions, compared with the row's wrap threshold before applying a whole step.
Eight projected depth indices selecting the water marks' current Y rows.
Fractional movement increments in the normal bank mode.
Alternate fractional movement increments used in the other projected bank mode.
Third set of fractional increments, selected when the bank constraint flag is active.
Fractional increments for the path which uses the self-modified signed one-byte drift.
Signed whole-pixel advance for each water mark when the lateral fraction wraps.
Eight per-mark positions within the depth update.
Per-mark mutable stage flags. The slot restart writes one at $1B7E.
Per-mark animation state reset when an existing mark is erased.
Previously drawn distance row for each of the eight water-mark slots.
Low address bytes used to erase the currently saved water-mark pixels.
High halves of the saved watermark pointers.
The low two bits of the lateral position, used to select the packed pixel alignment.
Temporary lateral coordinate for the water mark, checked before drawing a new bitmap slot.
Timer delaying the normal water-mark update while the course display is established.
Five little-endian addresses for repeated water-mark byte patterns, in the $1C30–$1C7F region.
High half alias of the five water-mark pointers.
Five groups of sixteen packed pixel bytes. The progression changes the position and width of the boundary between the $55 fill and the exposed area.
Sixteen packed bytes for the second marked phase at the address table's next entry.
Sixteen packed bytes for the middle boundary phase.
Penultimate sixteen-byte alignment of the water-mark boundary pixels.
Last sixteen-byte pattern in the water-mark address table.

Walks object slots seven down to four. For a slot with a variation enabled it toggles its state every twelve timer steps, then uses the object's type and variant tables to write the replacement slot bytes.
Mutable high byte of the first alternating object patch's store instruction. The reader selects it from $CDCF using the object type.
High address byte for the complementary alternating object's store. The same destination page table supplies it.
Eight per-object phase bits. A phase flip changes the Y adjustment used by $2359 and $C262.
Indexed by object code to get the first patch-list cursor used by the alternating state routine.
Object-indexed ending cursors for the reverse-running patch loop in $1C80.
Indexed offsets combined with the high destination byte chosen from $CDCF.
Bytes to install in the first state of the alternating object patch. Each shares an index with its destination offset at $1D7A.
Alternate value for each patch destination. The second state reads this table at $1CEA.
Per-slot state enabling the periodic patch. A zero bypasses it. Enabled entries alternate between one and two.
Eight countdown slots narrowed to objects four through seven by the variant updater.
Current slot in the outer reverse loop at $1C80.
Final cursor value for the current object's inner patch loop.
Starts the self-modified jump target at $139F, then advances it for each of four sprite Y coordinates in the interval $20–$7B. Called late in the playfield interrupt.

Opens a section by masking the course's next section selector to six bits. If the next three-byte event matches the current progress byte $6B, uses its operation byte to index $1FFB and passes the low nibble of its argument byte in X. Then advances the event pointer by three. When the timestamp does not match, the per-object dispatch uses $2069 instead.
Indirect jump through the two-byte handler address just assembled in zero page $60–$61.
Counter incremented by the raster course update when its movement condition holds.
Counter incremented in the playfield IRQ before the event progress update.
Low byte of the live pointer into the selected section's three-byte records.
High byte of the live pointer into the selected section's three-byte records.
Flag set after reading the section selector. Cleared by the next-section handler.
Type bytes for the per-sprite object slots. Zero means an inactive slot and other values index the object dispatch table.
Object code read for the extra update of sprite slot three.
Handler selector for sprite slot four, used in the dispatch at $1F6C.
Handler selector for the next projected object slot.
Current code for the update which receives Y equal to six.
Current code for the update of slot seven. The special trajectory path can activate it with $1E.
Event dispatch selector with Y equal to eight. Used for tunnel progress and special horizon changes.
Handler selector with Y equal to nine. Used for the companion side and special moving-object commands.
Per-slot impact or destruction flags. The update distinguishes a live sprite from one in its finishing animation.
Slot-four element of the sprite impact array, read directly by the left and right launch updates.
Little-endian dispatch table. The middle byte of each section event selects a handler through this table.
Alias for the high byte of entry zero in the adjacent dispatch table. The indexed load at $1F36 fetches the high byte of whichever two-byte entry $1F31 selected.
Little-endian dispatch table indexed by the active object codes in $1FEA–$1FF0. The dispatch supplies object element index 3 through 9 in Y.
Indexed high-byte alias for the active object dispatch table. The byte before it forms the low half of the first complete entry.
Bit masks used to clear the selected sprite's flag. The eight bytes run into the second mask array.
Indexed-mask alias at the start of sprite two's inverse bit.
Inverse sprite-three bit used directly by the missile flight path.
Enables a slot by ORing the corresponding entry into a sprite control shadow.
Direct mask for the missile slot's ninth horizontal bit.
Bit-seven entry of the sprite mask table. $AAF5 applies it to the X-MSB shadow. Indexed users also apply the table to expansion and multicolour.
Does no work and returns. Both event dispatch tables contain this address.
Calls $F797 to replenish the missile display, then jumps to $F71F, which writes colour $0A to $DBB1 and $DBB2.
Stores one into $20F4 and returns. This is the handler for section operation $2D.
Report outcome selector. Zero continues the course, and nonzero values choose a line sequence through $F274.
Handles section operation $2C. Clears $1FE6 and advances the course's section-selector pointer $02EB:$02EC.
Sets the horizon stream index to one and its initial delay to $27, then sets the active event to $29.
Clears the sprite pointer, selects a course-dependent colour and enables vertical expansion for the slot before completing its spawn record.
Selects shape $84 and colour eleven, then uses the common event parser to finish the slot.
Selects shape $84 and colour eight, clears the variation flag and clears the sprite X-MSB state before continuing the spawn.
Selects shape four and colour twelve, seeds placement from $B91D and marks the slot for its separate animation phase.
Installs shape $74 with colour two and enables variation, then seeds its placement from $B91D.
Selects sprite $74 with colour zero and takes the initial variant and lateral placement from the live selector at $B91D.
Extracts the high nibble of the event argument, then joins the common shape-$79 spawn path at $21B7.
Uses the live selector for placement, sets shape $79 and enables horizontal expansion for this slot.
Uses shape four and colour fourteen. When the event code is $32, reloads explicit placement from the argument instead of leaving the live-selector value.
If the state at $C1E6 is clear, selects shape $71 and derives placement from the sign and magnitude of $C4E9 through one of two tables.
Lateral placement for an object spawned while its parent's signed step is nonnegative.
Lateral placement for an object spawned while its parent's signed step is negative, indexed by half its magnitude.
Selects shape $71 with colour five before the shared slot initialiser.
Alternate colour setting for the same shape-$71 event family, with colour fourteen.
Selects shape $71 and colour two, seeds the live placement and joins the common late spawn path.
Chooses sprite pointer $80 and jumps into the shared course-dependent colour setup.
Chooses sprite pointer $7C, sets the alternate return instruction and chooses colour eleven in New Orleans or twelve otherwise.
Sets shape $0D, colour twelve and the variation flag. An explicit nonzero placement nibble in the event supersedes the default at $B91D.

Finishes assigning colour and variation state to the slot just selected. Decodes the event parameter's upper nibble, assigns type and initial depth, then adjusts colour and sprite flags for the new course object.
Writable byte set to the RTS opcode by the bridge sprite spawn path.

Sets sprite Y from the current depth entry. The object type and animation phase choose the projection offset. Updates animation pointers at depth milestones and either advances the cursor by two or clears the object when it reaches the end of the visible sequence.
Clears an object's low X byte, Y coordinate, type and three per-slot flags, then restores its multicolour bit. Y selects the slot.
Two stored zero bytes between the object update return and the following eight-slot flag array.
Per-slot flag used by $2359 to gate the Y adjustment in the variable projection state.
Projects the object's lateral screen position from its distance-row index and the river position arrays. Uses the displacement scale table at $8000 and writes sprite coordinates.
First sixteen values for placement variants. The projector copies the selected value to $2703.
Writable entry within the variant table. The type-$33 event replaces it with $20.
Next mutable placement entry. The type-$33 initialiser writes $38 before drawing its slot.
Mutable position entry which the type-$33 event sets to $50. A final variant follows at $26CA.
Sixteen per-variant signed adjustments loaded into $2705 for the current sprite.
Sixteen values selecting the negative or positive adjustment path for a projected object.
Per-slot lateral displacement accumulator modified by the object projection loop.
Final slot of the lateral accumulator, explicitly reset when starting the companion trajectory.
Per-slot fractional position. The row projection updates it before applying a whole step.
Slot seven's fractional position set to $A0 by the special object initialiser.
Saved depth steps for each sprite, initialised to $FF at spawn.
Final element of the previous depth array. Set to $FF when the slot begins a new motion sequence.
Current table-derived step size used when advancing a projected sprite.
Sign value from the variant direction table.
The current variant's row-related offset used in the drawing calculation.
Cleared by the panel setup while the briefing colours are installed.
Temporary difference between two depth observations used by the projection calculation.
Sets the alternate bank colour from $2727, sets $035F and installs $60 as the non-active depth on the normal side. Clears A before jumping to the paired state setup at $29A4.
Four course-specific colour entries for the first bank pair.
Alternate per-course colour family used when preparing the second projected approach.
Incremented when the near-bank sprite update can advance, then masked to test each fourth step.
Index derived from the active near-bank depth divided by eight.
Nonzero while the near-bank pair is in use. The update clears it at the terminal depth.
Divider for the companion sprite update, used to pace the far-bank redraw.
Active far-bank depth divided by eight, used for its sprite-patch range.
Nonzero while the far-bank pair is in use.
Start offsets for each of the seven progressive image replacements.
Exclusive limits for the replacement data written to the bank-pair sprites.
Per-phase spacing subtracted from one projected coordinate and applied to its companion sprite.
Per-slot initial position variant chosen by an event parameter or the live selector.
Last slot of the position-variant array. The special sprite release writes its active group's value here.
Eight cached placement lookups used by the object projector.
Per-sprite depth indices into the projected positions and frame progression.
Sets slot three's depth to $50 when the projectile meets a boundary.
Slot seven's projected depth, initialised to eight for the spawned object.
Eight auxiliary slot values cleared by the initialisation loop at $101B.
Slot index saved when the object routine temporarily reuses Y.

When the remaining segment count $27A8 is zero, reads the next packed turn byte through $02EF:$02F0. Low nibble is the duration. High nibble supplies the turn magnitude and direction, with $8–$F decoded as zero through minus seven.
Remaining course turn-segment duration. A zero lets $276C fetch and decode another packed byte.
Speed-indexed base steering correction. The bank logic halves it for the intermediate steering positions.
Screen codes for TOP and a blank before the adjacent AGENTS fragment.
Screen-code letters spelling AGENTS near the steering table. The last $FF precedes a returned instruction.
RTS instruction between the terminated text fragment and the following IRQ-mask helper.
Writes zero to the CIA1 interrupt control and $F0 to the VIC mask, then reenables CPU IRQ processing and returns.
First nine-entry increment table used by $A2EB to add to the pending counter at $EDF4. Mission distance progress also advances this counter at $14CF.
Second nine-entry increment table used by $A2F1 to load the other target display request.
32 pixel bytes for missile launch variant 0, selected by the pointer table at $A4C6. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.
32 pixel bytes for missile middle variant 0, selected by the pointer table at $A4D0. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.
32 pixel bytes for missile late variant 0, selected by the pointer table at $A4DA. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.
38 pixel bytes for missile launch variant 1, selected by the pointer table at $A4C6. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.

38 pixel bytes for missile late variant 1, selected by the pointer table at $A4DA. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.
38 pixel bytes for missile launch variant 2, selected by the pointer table at $A4C6. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.
38 pixel bytes for missile middle variant 2, selected by the pointer table at $A4D0. The drawing routine copies them into sprite slot $92 at $6480.
First screen-code stream used to supply an edge cell when the special horizon state shifts the first row.
Source of the edge character for the second shifted horizon row at $4517.
Source of the edge character for the third shifted row at $453F.
Clears the near-bank approach cursors and selects the course colour. Prepares two hires sprites, clears their shape buffer and records the active object's event code.
Thirteen-byte fragment between the near-bank initialiser's return and the course entry jump. It contains two absolute-store byte sequences adjacent to other residual bytes.
Jumps to $2B29, which selects course-dependent parameters before entering the gameplay update loop.

Sets initial gameplay variables and working arrays. Clears several $58-byte row arrays from $0400, seeds pairs of bitmap pointers from $83A8 and $9600, and fills $6A00 through $767F with $FF before the initial course drawing.
Picks four values from the course tables at $F000, $F005, $F014 and $F01C, then coordinates setup, river rendering and gameplay updates. Rejoins at $2B44 after $328F and $34CC.
Reads the speed index, falls through to drawing when it is nonzero and returns otherwise.
Jump into the clipped row-fill path at $2CBA.

Walks the distance rows using $50, constructs bitmap pointers from the split table at $8280 and $82D8, offsets them using $8200 and draws the bank edges with the four sub-byte masks at $3713 and $3717.

Chooses a row's lateral offset from the working geometry, then converts it to a bitmap pointer plus a two-bit pixel phase. Stamps the river-to-bank transition and fills outward up to an already matching byte.
Jumps to the row-pointer save path at $2EDC.
Branches to the bank fill decision at $2E66 before continuing the row routine.
Three cleared bytes between the river-row renderer and the next geometry state field.
Four zero bytes beginning with the workspace byte explicitly reset by $2A62.

Applies a pending curve orientation change and clears that request. For each of 88 distance rows, combines the live curvature offsets and fixed-point slope accumulators to rebuild four lateral boundary arrays at $0400, $0458, $04B0 and $0508.
Last applied orientation of the requested opposite-side geometry. Used to avoid applying the same orientation adjustment twice.
Walks the 88 distance rows backwards. Uses $05B8 and the row increments at $0560 to compute a per-row displacement into $0400.
Reconstructs two saved addresses for each distance row and writes multicolour byte $55 between them, stepping one eight-byte cell column at a time.
